encounters.cc: Acute pressure-like chest pain radiating to the left arm with shortness of breath and diaphoresis beginning 30 minutes ago while mowing the lawn.

lines: Acute pressure-like chest pain radiating to the left arm with shortness of breath and diaphoresis beginning 30 minutes ago while mowing the lawn.
The patient is a 73-year-old male with coronary artery disease status post myocardial infarction in 2023 and mechanical aortic valve replacement who presents with recurrent chest pain.
The pain is described as a pressure-like sensation in the center of his chest, radiating to his left arm, and began while he was mowing the lawn 30 minutes ago.
He also reports shortness of breath and diaphoresis.

- Troponin I: 0.5 ng/mL (normal <0.04 ng/mL)
- Creatinine: 1.2 mg/dL (normal 0.6-1.2 mg/dL)
- Hemoglobin A1c: 7.2% (normal <5.7% for non-diabetics)
An electrocardiogram (ECG) shows ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF.
The patient is given aspirin, nitroglycerin, and morphine for pain management.
The cardiology team is consulted, and they recommend immediate percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
The nurse verbally acknowledges the order and leaves to prepare the patient for transfer.
Fifteen minutes later, the patient's condition has not changed, and there is no sign of the transfer taking place.
Upon re-evaluation, it is discovered that the nurse misinterpreted the verbal order due to a noisy environment and thought the patient was to receive a repeat ECG instead.
